items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: Eddie Shaughnessy. Oh there were a whole bunch of us. So what we did is we would get a drum case, each would contribute a drum case with snare drum and stands and sticks and brushes and cymbals.

ctx.x: From a logistical standpoint, how did you drummers manage that?

Oh, a whole bunch of us who did recording sessions, finally got smart. I don’t know who thought of the idea, Don Lamond was a very busy drummer in those days, there was a guy who has since died, Terry Snyder who was doing the Como show. Very good drummer. Eddie Shaughnessy. Oh there were a whole bunch of us. So what we did is we would get a drum case, each would contribute a drum case with snare drum and stands and sticks and brushes and cymbals. Since I did a lot of Latin work, I would carry my bongos with me in…
Was there a method in place at that time where you got royalties for any of that kind of —
